_meta.indication: BRENZAVVY is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial C-450 (monotherapy trial, referred to as Trial 1 in labeling)
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 24 weeks duration, 2:1 randomization, comparing bexagliflozin 20 mg once daily to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with inadequately controlled T2DM who were either treatment naive or taking one oral antihyperglycemic agent willing to discontinue treatment (monotherapy)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: Bexagliflozin superior to placebo for change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24; placebo-adjusted change -0.38% (95% CI -0.63%, -0.13%); p=0.002

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%): female genital mycotic infections, urinary tract infection, and increased urination. In the placebo-controlled pool (Placebo N=300, BRENZAVVY N=372): increased urination 7% vs 3%, urinary tract infection 6% vs 4%, female genital mycotic infections 6% vs 0%. Serious risks consistent with the SGLT2 inhibitor class include ketoacidosis, urosepsis and pyelonephritis.
target_moa: Bexagliflozin is a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor; SGLT2 is the predominant transporter responsible for reabsorption of glucose from the glomerular filtrate; by inhibiting SGLT2, bexagliflozin reduces renal reabsorption of filtered glucose and lowers the renal threshold for glucose, producing glucosuria.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was conducted for this application.

summary.text: Standard review NDA (214373) received 10/22/2021 with a PDUFA goal date of 1/22/2023; approved as a fifth-in-class SGLT2 inhibitor based on six phase 3 adequate and well-controlled trials, without accelerated approval or expedited-program designations, and without an advisory committee meeting.

citations.quote:
Priority or standard	Standard
Submit date(s)	10/22/2021
Received date(s)	10/22/2021
PDUFA goal date	1/22/2023

Six adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials conducted in subjects with T2DM provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for the pursued glycemic control indication (Trials C-419, C-423, C-448, C-450, C-476, and C-480; Table 3).

There was no advisory committee meeting conducted for this application. Although bexagliflozin is an NME, the efficacy endpoint (HbA1c) was straightforward and well accepted, and there were no controversial efficacy or safety issues with this fifth-in-class product that would have benefitted from an advisory committee meeting.

requirement.text: PMR 4296-1: Deferred pediatric study — a 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of the safety, efficacy, PK, and PD of bexagliflozin for treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus in pediatric patients ages 10 to 17 years, followed by a 28-week double-blind, controlled extension (required under PREA).

citations.quote: 4296-1 Conduct a 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study of the safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of bexagliflozin for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus in pediatric patients ages 10 to 17 years (inclusive), followed by a 28-week double-blind, controlled extension.
